text:
maya: Heads-up — noticed a sharp uptick in 429s from a handful of API keys around 18:42 UTC. Grafana shows 429 rate moving from ~0.5% -> ~6% in ~3m. Filing thread to propose alert tuning + quick mitigation steps.
jonathan: Can you paste the query? Is this per-org or per-key?
maya: it's per-key. Query: `sum(rate(http_responses{code=\"429\"}[5m])) by (api_key)`; top keys show short spikes. Also token/sec for same keys increased.
kevin: Hmm. Are these bursty short spikes or sustained? If short, we should avoid paging SRE for every incident.
maya: most are 1-2m bursts but very high peak. CS has customer logs — they were migrating and opened many parallel connections.
cs_sara: Customer reported ~10m slowdown; they were running parallel workers without jitter. They asked whether we can auto-throttle.
jonathan: Proposal: two-tier alerting and a non-blocking mitigation path: 
  - WARN (no page): 5m window, 429-rate > 3% AND traffic from single api_key > 100 rps.
  - PAGE: 15m sustained 429-rate > 2% AND single-key > 200 rps, OR org-wide 429-rate > 1% for 15m.
kevin: +1. Also a short-term burst alert: 1m window >8% 429s -> fire a high-severity but non-paging message to ops_channel and run the automated soft-throttle.
maya: Runbook snippet suggestion:
```
1) Open Grafana: /d/ops/429-spikes
2) Run quick prom query: `curl -s "http://metrics-query/?q=sum(rate(http_responses{code=\"429\"}[1m])) by (api_key)`
3) Identify top api_key(s). If single key >8% => consider soft-throttle.
4) Soft-throttle command: `POST /internal/admin/throttle?key=<key>&rate=50/s&duration=60s` (applies token-bucket).
5) If multiple keys or org-wide spike -> consider routing policy change: move traffic to secondary pool / fallback to smaller model variant.
6) Notify CS and apply customer-facing template.
```
cs_sara: Can we auto-apply a short soft-throttle (non-blocking) on offending key for 30s and send customer note? That'd often stop the cascade.
jonathan: We can. Automation idea: detect >500 rps + 429-rate >5% in 1m -> apply 5s token-bucket throttle repeatedly for 60s and send note to #cs-alerts.
kevin: Need to watch for false positives from scheduled jobs/cron spikes. Add tag-based filtering and an ignore list for internal/internal-service keys.
maya: Agreed. Also request adding telemetry fields: `client_rate_limit_policy` and `throttle_action` labels in logs/metrics so we can measure impact.
kevin: For the alert rules I'll propose PromQL examples:
```
# warn (no page)
( sum(rate(http_responses{code=\"429\"}[5m])) by (api_key) / sum(rate(http_requests[5m])) by (api_key) ) > 0.03 and sum(rate(http_requests[5m])) by (api_key) > 100
# page
( sum(rate(http_responses{code=\"429\"}[15m])) by (api_key) / sum(rate(http_requests[15m])) by (api_key) ) > 0.02 and sum(rate(http_requests[15m])) by (api_key) > 200
```
jonathan: Also add a synthetic check: per-key RPS sampling every 30s to detect sudden jump from baseline >5x. That catches new-onset floods.
cs_sara: I'll create a short CS template and an FAQ snippet about client-side exponential backoff + jitter and parallelism limits.
alertbot: Incident-bot: New alert created: `ENGSRE-BURST-WARN` (id: 4478) - severity: warning, no paging. Created by maya.
maya: I'll draft the Grafana alert + update runbook page. Assigning automation to @kevin and CS template to @cs_sara. I'll also add an ignore-list for internal keys.
kevin: I'll implement the soft-throttle automation and ignore-list this week. Will open PR for the internal admin endpoint change.
cs_sara: I'll draft the customer-facing message and send to legal for a quick check.
maya: Thanks all. If no objections I'll roll alerts and automation Tuesday during the quiet window. :thumbsup:
jonathan: SGTM.
kevin: SG.
cs_sara: 👍
